(Code 1967, § 27-29; Ord. No. 723, § 1, 8-20-1996)
1387:
(a) The wastewater characteristics which are used to determine user charge are (i) BOD, (ii) suspended solids, (iii) flow volume and (iv) grease. Normal wastewater discharges and industrial wastewater discharges of normal strength wastewaters shall be charged a basic user charge in which flow volume is the wastewater characteristic for determining the charge. When BOD, suspended solids, or grease concentrations in a user's wastewater discharge is in excess of the range of concentration in normal strength wastewater, a surcharge shall be made to the base charge.
(b) The formula for determining basic user charge which applies to normal strength discharges shall be as follows:
R = Vm Ct
Where:
R | = | Monthly user charge
Vm | = | Monthly volume contribution from a user in 1,000-gallon units
Ct | = | Basic unit charge to user (dollar per 1,000 gallons for operation and maintenance)
(c) When BOD, suspended solids and grease exceed the range of concentration of those pollutants in normal strength wastewater, a surcharge shall be added to the basic charge. The surcharge shall be determined as follows:
Cs = 0.000692 (Bc × B + Sc × S + Gc × G) Vu
Where:
Cs | = | Surcharge for wastewater (dollars per month)
Bc | = | Operation and maintenance costs for treatment of a pound of BOD
B | = | Concentration of BOD from a user above base load (mg/l)
Sc | = | Operation and maintenance costs for treatment of a pound of suspended solids
S | = | Concentration of suspended solids from a user above base level (mg/l)
Gc | = | Operation and maintenance cost for treatment of a pound of grease
G | = | Concentration of grease from a user above base level (mg/l)
Vu | = | Flow volume in units of 1,000 gallons per year
(d) Unit value determination.
(1) The basic unit Ct, which shall be revised biennially, shall be determined as follows:
Ct = (Bd Bc + Sd Sc + Gd Gc + Vt)
Where:
Ct | = | As defined in subsection (b) of this section
B | = | Average pounds of BOD per 1,000 gallons of normal strength wastewater contributed
Sd | = | Average pounds of suspended solids per 1,000 gallons of normal strength wastewater contributed.
Sc | = | As defined in subsection (c) of this section
Gd | = | Average pounds of grease per 1,000 gallons of normal strength wastewater contributed.
Gc | = | As defined in subsection (c) of this section
Vt | = | The operation and maintenance costs for transportation and treatment of 1000 gallons of wastewater.
(2) Bd, Sd and Gd shall be revised not less frequently than biannually and shall be determined by dividing actual wastewater treatment plant loading less total surcharged loading by total annual volume contribution by domestic wastewater dischargers.
(3) Bc, Sc and Gc shall be revised not less often than two years by dividing their respective annual maintenance and operation costs by their respective annual loadings.
(4) Wastewater monitoring and reporting shall be as described in division 6 of this article.
(5) Wastewater discharge volume (Vm) for dischargers of normal strength wastewater shall be 100 percent of the amount of water metered. For industrial wastewater dischargers which discharge surcharged waste the wastewater discharge volume (Vu) shall be 80 percent of the amount of water metered unless it can be shown that the volume of wastewater discharge is less.
(Code 1967, § 27-295; Ord. No. 723, § 1, 8-20-1996)
1388:
(a) The city has implemented the user charge system as approved by the director of the environmental protection division on August 22, 1980. User charges will be based on actual operation and maintenance costs. User charges shall be reviewed biannually and revised to reflect actual treatment plant works' operation and maintenance cost.
(b) The city shall document the various waste treatment plant loading categories and the operation and maintenance costs attributable to each category, record user charge revenues and demonstrate that the user charge derived is a proportional distribution of operation and maintenance costs.
(Code 1967, § 27-296; Ord. No. 723, § 1, 8-20-1996)
1389:

(1) A general review of operating records with particular emphasis on the impact of industrial flows.
(2) An inspection and review of the facilities to identify any significant needs for maintenance or replacement.
